steps.title: Overlapping groups
steps.intro: Two question types: a range (min and max) or an exact overlap.

tables.title: Range questions
head: What
Rule
Example
rows: \((A+B)-\text{total}\), or \(0\) if that is not positive

tips: Two shares adding to exactly the whole do NOT force an overlap; more than the whole does.
"Distinct items in either collection" is the union — neither is 0.

steps.stem: Of 45 campers, 28 bring a torch, 23 bring a map, and 16 bring both. How many bring neither?
explanation: Sixteen are in the shared region. Map-only campers number twenty-three minus sixteen, or seven. The twenty-eight torch owners already include the shared region, so adding only the seven new map owners gives thirty-five with at least one item. Ten of the forty-five so have neither.
We could also find torch-only as twelve and add twelve, sixteen, and seven. That is valid, but it is not necessary if we already know the combined torch total.

steps.stem: A workshop has 22 machines. Fourteen cut, twelve polish, and three do neither. How many both cut and polish?
explanation: Three outside both groups leave nineteen machines doing at least one job. The two job totals add to twenty-six. The excess twenty-six minus nineteen is the seven counted in both groups.

steps.stem: The people who both volunteer and study photography make up \(\frac16\) of the photography students and \(\frac14\) of all volunteers. What is the ratio of photography students who do not volunteer to volunteers who do not study photography?
explanation: Call the overlap one unit. If that is one sixth of photography students, the full photography group is six units. If it is one quarter of volunteers, the full volunteer group is four units.
Remove the shared unit from each group. Photography-only is five units and volunteering-only is three. Their ratio is five to three. We never need the size of the group that does neither.

steps.stem: At a community event with 240 guests, 35% know the organizer and 80% know the host. What is the minimum number who know both?
explanation: The group percentages add to 115%. The event has only 100% distinct guests, so at least fifteen percentage points represent people counted in both groups. Fifteen percent of 240 is twenty-four plus twelve, or thirty-six.
This is a minimum because we can place all twenty percent who do not know the host inside the organiser group. The remaining fifteen percent of the organiser group must then know the host too.

steps.stem: A class has 48 students. Twenty-one work in the greenhouse and eleven work in the orchard. Which could be the number who work in neither place?
explanation: The smallest union is twenty-one, achieved if all eleven orchard workers also work in the greenhouse. That leaves at most twenty-seven in neither. The largest union is thirty-two, achieved if the groups are disjoint, leaving at least sixteen in neither.
So the neither count ranges from sixteen to twenty-seven. Eighteen is the only listed value inside this range. It can occur when the overlap is two: the union is 21+11−2=30, leaving eighteen.

steps.stem: Of a company’s employees, \(\frac25\) can code, \(\frac45\) work remotely, \(\frac15\) are juniors, and \(\frac12\) are in training. Which statement is not necessarily true?
choices: At least one non-junior cannot code
At least one junior works remotely
At least one coder works remotely
At least one trainee cannot code
explanation: Coders plus remote employees give \(\frac25+\frac45=\frac65>1\), forcing overlap. Trainees plus non-coders give \(\frac12+\frac35>1\), also forcing overlap. Non-juniors plus non-coders give \(\frac45+\frac35>1\), again forcing overlap.

Juniors and remote employees add to exactly one: \(\frac15+\frac45=1\). They can occupy separate groups with no overlap. Equality with the whole does not force a shared member, so the junior-and-remote statement is the one not guaranteed.

steps.stem: At lunch, \(\frac25\) of the staff choose soup, \(\frac14\) choose salad, and \(\frac1{10}\) choose both. Exactly 8 people choose both. How many choose neither?
explanation: One tenth of the staff equals eight, so the full staff total is eighty. Soup is two fifths of eighty, or thirty-two; salad is one quarter, or twenty. Their union is 32+20−8=44. The remaining thirty-six choose neither.
Finding the total first turns the later overlap work into whole-number arithmetic. This can be simpler than subtracting several fractions and then converting the answer.

steps.stem: Two researchers photograph different butterflies. One photographs 31 butterflies and the other 22. Together their photographs show 40 distinct butterflies. How many butterflies appear in both collections?
explanation: The forty butterflies are the ones shown in at least one collection. They are the union, not every butterfly in the habitat. Relative to this stated set, the neither region is zero.
Adding thirty-one and twenty-two gives fifty-three collection memberships. The thirteen extra memberships come from butterflies counted once in each collection. Thus thirteen appear in both.

steps.stem: At a fair, 150 different people each win one prize. Of the winners, 65% live nearby and 55% arrived by train. What is the minimum number who both live nearby and arrived by train?
explanation: The two group sizes add to 65%+55%=120% of all winners. Only 100% distinct people are available, so at least 20% were counted twice. Twenty percent of 150 is 30.

steps.stem: Every one of a group of students studies art, music, or both. There are 26 art students, 19 music students, and 11 who study both. How many students are in the group?
explanation: Adding 26 and 19 counts the eleven students in both courses twice. Remove one copy of those eleven: 26+19−11=34.

steps.stem: A firm gives one company tablet to each of \(\frac35\) of its employees, using 72 tablets. Half of all employees also own a personal tablet. What is the minimum number with both a company and a personal tablet?
explanation: Seventy-two is three fifths of the workforce, so one fifth is twenty-four and the total is 120. Personal-tablet owners number sixty. The smallest overlap is 72+60−120=12.

steps.stem: Of 120 hikers, 54 carry a map, 82 carry a compass, and 31 carry both. How many carry neither?
explanation: The number carrying at least one item is 54+82−31=105. Subtract from the full group: 120−105=15.

steps.stem: In a town, \(\frac35\) of residents cycle, \(\frac14\) grow vegetables, \(\frac25\) keep pets, and \(\frac45\) are under 50. Which of the following overlaps necessarily contains at least one resident?
choices: Residents aged at least 50 who grow vegetables
explanation: Under-50 residents and pet owners together make \(\frac45+\frac25=\frac65\) of the population. Since this exceeds one, some must be in both groups. The other pairs add to at most one, so they could be disjoint.

steps.stem: Sixty trainees score between 0 and 12 (inclusive). Twenty-six score from 9 to 12 (inclusive), twenty-four from 7 to 10 (inclusive), and twenty score below 7. How many score from 9 to 10 (inclusive)?
explanation: The two listed bands cover every score from 7 to 12, so their union has 60−20=40 trainees. Their common band is 9 to 10. Its size is 26+24−40=10.

steps.stem: Of 250 students, 205 enjoy chess and 190 play a musical instrument. What is the greatest possible percentage who neither enjoy chess nor play an instrument?
explanation: The union cannot be smaller than the larger group, which has 205 students. It can equal 205 if all 190 musicians also enjoy chess. This leaves 250−205=45 in neither group. Forty-five out of 250 is 18%.

steps.stem: Every member of a club speaks Spanish, Italian, or both. Spanish speakers are \(\frac34\) of the club and Italian speakers are \(\frac58\). What fraction speaks both?
explanation: Because everyone is in at least one group, the overlap is \(\frac34+\frac58-1=\frac68+\frac58-\frac88=\frac38\).

steps.stem: A class has 48 students. Twenty-eight swim and twenty-four cycle. Three quarters of the cyclists also swim. How many students do neither activity?
explanation: Three quarters of twenty-four is eighteen. The union is 28+24−18=34, leaving 48−34=14 in neither group.

steps.stem: Of a shop’s bags, \(\frac23\) are blue, \(\frac34\) have zips, and \(\frac12\) are both blue and zipped. What is the ratio of blue bags without zips to zipped bags that are not blue?
explanation: Blue without zips is \(\frac23-\frac12=\frac16\). Zipped but not blue is \(\frac34-\frac12=\frac14\). Their ratio is \(\frac16:\frac14=2:3\).

steps.stem: A survey of 90 people finds that 48 use buses and 57 use trains. What is the range of possible numbers using both?
explanation: The minimum is 48+57−90=15. The maximum is the smaller group, forty-eight, because everyone in that group could also belong to the larger one. Both endpoints are possible.

steps.stem: Among 64 visitors, 39 enter the gallery, 31 enter the garden, and 12 enter neither. How many enter exactly one of the two places?
explanation: The union is 64−12=52. Both is 39+31−52=18. Exactly one is 52−18=34.

steps.stem: In a group of 100 readers, 70 read fiction, 65 read history, and 60 read science. What is the minimum possible number who read all three?
explanation: A person can belong to two groups without belonging to all three. One hundred people could so supply two hundred memberships without any triple overlap. The required total is only 195, so zero may be possible. We still need a construction to confirm it.

steps.stem: A school has 80 pupils. Fifty study French, forty study German, and twenty-five study both. Of the pupils who study French, what fraction also study German?
explanation: The phrase “of the pupils who study French” makes fifty the denominator. Twenty-five of those fifty also study German, so the fraction is one half.

steps.stem: In a team, 55% can code and 45% can design. Twenty percent do neither. What percentage can do both?
explanation: If twenty percent do neither, eighty percent do at least one. The group percentages add to one hundred percent, so the excess over the union is twenty percent. That excess is the overlap.

steps.stem: A bag contains 72 badges. Forty-eight are round and thirty are metal. At least how many round badges are not metal?
explanation: To make round-but-not-metal as small as possible, put all thirty metal badges among the forty-eight round badges. That still leaves 48−30=18 round badges that are not metal.

steps.stem: Of 150 employees, 90 work remotely at least once a week, 75 work flexibly, and 60 do both. How many do exactly one of these?
explanation: Remote only is 90−60=30. Flexible only is 75−60=15. Add them to get 45 people with exactly one arrangement.
